subject: Specific 'shape' symbols appear incorrectly (diamonds vs circles)

messages.author: 92a46c9449c605e2
messages.subject: Specific 'shape' symbols appear incorrectly (diamonds vs circles)
parts:
Hello,

Using R 2.14.0, I've written some code that should render points with
a circular shape but that appear as diamonds. The shape codes I'm
using are 1 and 16 ('empty' and 'filled' circles), but what I'm
getting appears more like codes 5 and 18 ('empty' and 'filled'
diamonds).

Any idea as to why this might be? My code is below.

x <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg, color=factor(am),
shape=factor(gear)))
x <- x + geom_point()
x + scale_shape_manual(values= c('3'= 1, '4' = 16, '5' = 4))

Many thanks,
Mauricio

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Specific 'shape' symbols appear incorrectly (diamonds vs circles)
parts:
I think this was fixed in the development version:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/264

But you can also use this:
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=wt, y=mpg, color=factor(am), shape=factor(gear))) + 
  geom_point() + scale_shape_manual(breaks=c(3,4,5), values= c(1,16,4))

Just make sure that the breaks are in ascending order -- there's another bug that's yet to be fixed, where it doesn't work correctly when the breaks are specified in another order.
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/issues/501

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Specific 'shape' symbols appear incorrectly (diamonds vs circles)
parts:
Hm, it's possible that you're running into an issue with non-antialiased graphical output. That is, the shapes are circles, but they may look like diamonds due to poor quality graphical output. Does it look right when you output to pdf?

-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Specific 'shape' symbols appear incorrectly (diamonds vs circles)
parts:
If you output to png using cairo, that should work. If you're using Windows, you might have to install some packages - but I don't a Windows computer so I can't say for sure. Maybe someone else with Windows experience can explain?

png("myfile.png", type="cairo")
# ggplot...
dev.off()

For screen antialiased screen output, on a Mac you can do:
quartz()
# ggplot...

On Linux:
x11(type="cairo")
# ggplot...

Again, on Windows, I'm not sure.

-Winston
